## Post-market (live)
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**URL:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9_eSvyc2VFE  
**Duration:** ~8:33  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-07-20-post.md`

### What happened / what he did
- **Huge gap-down** across indices (news-driven) — pre chart plan discarded; wait for **first momentum**.
- Open chop → brief recovery → second candle selling. Waited; then thesis: gap-down + news → **sellers tempt** into puts with nearby SLs → need a **retracement/recovery**, not continuous 1000-pt dump.
- Bought **calls** (Sensex ~900, Nifty ~1430) to capture seller-flush recovery; held through early MTM loss.
- Booked once a solid recovery / average target hit. Explicit: trade was **not** from prior-day buyers sitting — inventory had cleared; live **seller SL** psychology drove the call.

### Process lessons
- Large news gap-down **resets** structure; don’t force yesterday’s inventory map.
- Continuous dump with no pause = possible runaway → take loss; choppy sell after big gap = sellers to flush → recovery trade.
- Entry after SLs form nearby, not into the first panic candle.

### Keep permanently
1. Huge gap-down + news → structure reset; wait first tape, then decide recovery vs runaway.
2. After big gap-down, clustered **seller** SLs often need a flush → recovery can be the trade (not “buy yesterday’s buyers”).
3. If momentum is continuous one-way with no retrace, treat as runaway and respect the loss path.

### Day-specific only
- Qty and exact ~500 closing/round interaction are session-specific.

## Post-market (live)
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**URL:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0HnoI5CMaFE  
**Duration:** ~8:44  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-07-21-post.md`

### What happened / what he did
- **Flat** open then upside; BN led → quick **calls** (~200 BN call noted, Sensex ~900, Nifty ~1430) to beat late crowd.
- Thesis matched pre: no held inventory after both-side day → follow open; flat often lifts first to tempt both sides.
- BN then rejected hard through ~**58,000**; companions lagged. Held to loss limit then **cut** when direction flipped and BN broke down (late buyers got invited on the dip — edge died).

### Process lessons
- Unclear inventory → open-type follow is correct process even when the day loses.
- Don’t over-trust a lone BN sprint while Nifty/Sensex fail closing levels.
- Deep retrace that invites fresh buyers against your long = thesis kill → cut at limit.

### Keep permanently
1. Both-side prior day → assume **cleared hold inventory**; bias = open type, not forced counter-trade.
2. Flat after messy day: first lift can be the plan, but deep invite-the-buyers pullback invalidates.
3. Cut when companions fail and your lead index breaks the mapped hold.

### Day-specific only
- Exact qty and 58k path are session-specific.

### What happened / what he did
- **Gap-up** (Sensex/Nifty even larger) + mild rejection.
- Because inventory unclear, **followed ongoing cover** → **bought** (calls) rather than shorting the gap.
- Risk: oversized gap-up can suck in FOMO buyers then flip fully negative — watched for **fast rejection**.
- BN lagged initially then joined upside; average target reached → **booked** as time passed and momentum stayed slow/sideways.
- Explicit: no clear buyer/seller SL pools → follow market, don’t invent a counter-trade.

- Confusion days → trade **with** the existing recovery, not against it.
- Large gap-up increases trap risk even on longs — don’t overstay.
- Average target + slow tape + lots of time = book.

1. If you can’t identify inventory, default to **following the active regime**.
2. Gap size changes risk even when direction bias is buy.

2. Avoid runaway gap-up chases even when you wanted to sell elsewhere.

## Post-market (live)
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**URL:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpK2h9xsrXk  
**Duration:** ~9:01

### What happened / what he did
- Pre-open looked **flat**; planned **positive / buy** if open momentum confirms.
- Risk called: sudden **large selling** at open implies market wants to stay in range → bad for longs.
- Opened with positive momentum → bought calls (Sensex ~840, Nifty ~1365; BN size implied in flow).
- Thesis: prior breakout attracted buyers who got rejected/flushed; then slow cover → **don’t target those buyers**; flat/small gap-up → **go with upside**.
- Also discussed: market doesn’t hunt *your* SL personally — it hunts **clustered** retail SLs.
- Trade went to loss as rejection matched the prior cover; held while thesis alive, then **cut** when continuous selling + Sensex/Nifty joined downside and **loss limit** hit.
- Post-mortem: breakout-then-flush buyers thesis failed when market sold straight through — no point “thinking” a wrong trade.

### Process lessons
- Wait for first open momentum when range is messy; don’t force before tape speaks.
- Pre-calculate risk; exit at limit without storytelling.
- SL-cluster psychology ≠ “market is out to get me.”
- Wrong trade + accelerating sell = cut; don’t average hope.

### Keep permanently
1. Range days: large open sell = range warning; small pullback + breakout attempt can still be buy.
2. Flush-then-cover maps need the market to **hold**; if it sells through your limit, exit.
3. Personalize risk math, not personalize “SL hunting.”

## Post-market (live)
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-08-04-post.md`

### What happened / what he did
- **Gap-up** open; still planned **sell / put-side** to target buyers (contrast with Aug 3 — see below).
- Entry cue: wait for **closing-price breakdown** (BN + Sensex). Until then buyers don’t start cutting; small retrace noise is expected.
- Put book discussed: BN **57,800** + **57,700** (same qty), Sensex **78,700** put, Nifty expiry qty ~**1430**.
- Volatile / expiry day → wider target **and** SL tolerance mentioned — still not “hold forever.”
- Trade flicked profit ↔ loss while hovering near closing price; chop invited late risk-takers.
- Retrace ran higher, **especially Bank Nifty** → thesis (need CP breakdown) failing in real time.

### Trade outcome
- **Loss / trade cut** — put-side sell after gap-up; **not** held to target.
- Cut when **Bank Nifty started rising** against the put thesis; no point holding a bigger loss hoping for delayed breakdown.
- Nifty/Sensex mild bounce might have been handleable; **BN leading higher** was the kill signal.

### Why gap-up sell today vs gap-up buy Aug 3
| Factor | Aug 3 (buy with gap-up) | Aug 4 (sell buyers on gap-up) |
|--------|-------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Holiday in between | Yes (risk-off → thinner fresh inventory / different map) | **No** holiday between |
| Prior close | Retracement into close | **Exact round-number support** hold across indices |
| Inventory read | Soft open → hunt buyers; solid gap-up → ride | Buyers sat on round numbers → gap-up still hunt, but wait **closing-price breakdown** |

### Process lessons
- After continued upside without ATH/explosive special case → buyers are the target; sell setups on gap-up / flat / normal gap-down; ignore large gap-down.
- Same shape open ≠ same plan — holiday + retrace-close vs exact round-number hold flips gap-up buy vs sell.
- Sell-the-buyers after gap-up needs **closing-price breakdown** before buyers start cutting.
- If BN leads higher against puts → **cut**; don’t hold for a larger loss.
- Volatile/expiry: wider target/SL ok — still respect cut discipline when the leader invalidates.

### Keep permanently
1. Normal continuation (not ATH / not explosive) → buyers are hunt targets; gap-up / flat / normal gap-down = sell map; **ignore large gap-down**.
2. Holiday-in-between + retrace close → gap-up often **buy with market**; no holiday + exact round-number support hold → gap-up can still **sell buyers**, but wait for **closing-price breakdown**.
3. Put thesis: if **Bank Nifty leads higher** → cut; don’t hold a big loss hoping.

### Day-specific only
- Exact strikes (57800/57700, 78700), Nifty ~1430 qty, and “wider SL because expiry/volatile” sizing are session-specific.

## Post-market (live)
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-08-05-post.md`

### What happened / what he did
- **Good gap-up**, then rejection ↔ buying flicker — still planned **sell / put-side** (not a seller hunt).
- Put book: BN **57,800** put qty **1170**; Sensex qty **900**; Nifty qty **1430**.
- Thesis: first sharp down after a **positive / gap-up trend** → retail can’t sell much; those who did often **book targets** → **thin sellers** → **don’t hunt them**. If gap-up continues with **only buyers** left → **sell more likely**.
- Big gap leaves little room to trap sellers then squeeze up.
- Sensex/Nifty printed profit first; BN lagged then joined. Watch BN near **~58,000** round number on puts (breakout risk with larger BN size).
- Mindset while both buyers and sellers still participate → profit safer; when **only one side** remains → danger.

### Trade outcome
- **PROFIT** — put-side after gap-up; booked a **good profit**.
- Reflected on Aug 4: almost staying would have worked later (market fell from near exit), but **BN rising was the correct cut-by-rule** — follow the rule, not hindsight.
- After prior-day loss, took a solid profit when available rather than stretching for a huge day.

### Why sell on gap-up (not hunt day-1 sellers)
| Factor | Read |
|--------|------|
| Prior tape | First real sell after positive/gap-up stretch |
| Retail inventory | Sellers thin / small qty; many already booked |
| Gap-up continuation | If only buyers pile in → downside more likely than a clean seller squeeze |
| vs seller hunt | No need to hunt thin day-1 sellers — **sell with** the structure instead |

### Process lessons
- After first big sell day into a prior uptrend: sellers thin → **don’t hunt them** on the next gap-up; prefer **sell** if gap continues with only buyers.
- Large gap-up reduces room for the classic trap-then-squeeze of shorts.
- Put book: BN near round number (~58,000) is the risk focus when size is heaviest there.
- While both sides still participate, hold thesis; one-sided tape → protect profit.
- Process over hindsight: Aug 4 BN-lead cut was correct by rule even if price later fell from the exit area.
- After a loss day, **book** when a good profit is available — don’t demand maximum momentum.

### Keep permanently
1. First sharp sell after positive/gap-up trend → retail sellers thin (book targets) → **don’t hunt them**; if next gap-up continues with **only buyers** → **sell** more likely.
2. Big gap leaves little room to trap shorts then squeeze — don’t invent that path.
3. Puts with heavy BN size: watch **round-number** breakout risk (e.g. ~58,000).
4. Both sides still in → profit safer; **only one side** left → danger / tighten.
5. Prior-day loss → when good profit appears, **book**; don’t stretch for a “huge” day.
6. Cut-by-rule (BN lead against puts) stays correct even if later tape would have worked — process > hindsight.

### Day-specific only
- Exact strikes/qty (57800 put 1170, Sensex 900, Nifty 1430) and the ~58,000 BN watch are session-specific.

## Live / IH post
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-08-07-post.md`

### What happened / what he did (chronological)

**Open & wait**
- **Light gap-down**. Sensex and Nifty showed early **recovery / slight positive** right after open → **wait** briefly (don’t force sell into the bounce).
- Overall still planned selling, but open was drifting positive → pause.
- BN chart looked **ready sooner** for a put entry; still waited a bit for Sensex/Nifty alignment.

**Entry**
- After a short wait: if market goes **further up**, it risks becoming **too positive** → enter puts now.
- BN chart “bilkul sahi”; Sensex/Nifty might give more trouble — **breakout should not** happen; the little upside that was due had already printed.
- Puts: BN **57,900** + **57,800**; Sensex qty **900**; Nifty qty **1430**.
- Early flick: small loss ↔ profit noise — expected.

**Why sell / put (thesis)**
- Prior day (Aug 6): gap-up + continued positive; momentum small but market went **above 58,000** and stayed constructive → **sellers not sitting**; **buyers** are the inventory.
- Light GD → hunt those buyers with puts.
- Early bounce after GD is **bait**: if market dumped straight from the open, buyers might exit in 2–3 minutes; a small recovery gives them **hope** → they **average** / hold → then market delivers a **bigger loss** to them. That average-then-flush is the path being followed.
- Same read on Sensex: prior gap-up / hold-up → buyers, not sellers.
- Same on Nifty: small prior momentum but held **up** → buyers sitting.
- After bait + flush of anyone who tried early sells → overall selling should land; capture it with puts.
- Broader frame: market was going up ~2 days, rejection, then continued → sellers already flushed earlier → **buyers** remain → target them. Selling *will* come (small or large); puts are there to capture it.

**Invalidation / mid-trade risk**
- If price **crosses closing price** → market turns positive and the put is **wrong** (buyers already got their bait bounce; further upside = thesis fail). Prefer fall **before** CP cross.
- Mid: loss started increasing as BN pushed up and SN/Nifty went positive briefly — watched CP carefully.
- Then **Sensex/Nifty started giving profit first**; BN still showed some loss — not a big problem, because the SN/Nifty drop from their highs was the right shape (if they had crossed CP, market could have gone too positive).

**Psychology / resistance ignore**
- Question: if CP is resistance, won’t others sell there? Unlikely — traders who sold into this chart already took repeated losses; mindset after **repeated ups** is “where do I **buy**?” — GD recovery focused them on buying. **Resistance ignored**; buyers add; gradual fall pays the puts.

**Momentum, sideways, target expand**
- BN then joined the sell; SN/Nifty already negative → profit expanding. Wait for target **unless sideways**.
- Sideways is only knowable **after a breakdown** fails to appear — until breakdown, don’t declare sideways. Momentum market: no breakdown → maybe sideways; wait for momentum.
- Strong multi-index sell (all three trying down together) → **expand target**; easier to achieve.

**Second bait → book**
- Mid-move: market paused / bait again — gives remaining buyers hope that “breakdown isn’t coming” (they may not even add size, but hope keeps them in for a **larger loss**).
- Expect **one more momentum leg** → that leg is the **book** zone. Don’t fear the temporary profit dip during the bait pause.
- Booked on that second momentum: smooth mapped sell already paid; more move possible but not required.
- Closing recap: buyers averaged on the GD bounce bait → then large loss; early put loss then fast target once momentum started; **PROFIT jabardast**.

### Trade outcome (IH)
- **PROFIT** — put-side after light gap-down; early bait bounce held through; smooth 3-index sell → expanded target booked; **very good / jabardast**.

### Why light GD put (buyer hunt) worked
| Factor | Read |
|--------|------|
| Prior tape (Aug 6) | Gap-up + hold **above 58k** / positive → buyers sat, sellers gone |
| Open | Light GD = enough to hunt buyers (distance from RN helps) |
| Early bounce | **Bait to average** — hope → bigger loss later (vs instant dump = quick buyer exit) |
| Invalidation | **Closing-price cross** = put wrong |
| Mid | SN/Nifty profit first; BN lags then joins; expand target on smooth 3-index sell |
| Book | Second momentum after mid-move bait pause |

### Process lessons
- After positive hold-up / buyers sitting: need a **decent GD** (farther from RN better) to hunt; flat/GU → buy with market — don’t blanket-sell every soft open.
- Light GD bounce after buyers sat is often **bait to average** — don’t treat the recovery as thesis-kill if CP still holds; instant dump would have flushed buyers fast; bait creates the larger loss path.
- Put invalidation: **closing-price cross** = trade wrong; prefer fall before that.
- Companions (SN/Nifty) can lead profit while BN lags — not automatic cut if the CP map still holds.
- After repeated upside days, retail mindset is “where to buy?” — resistance ignored; that supports the gradual sell path.
- Sideways only knowable after breakdown fails — don’t declare chop early; wait momentum.
- Smooth 3-index sell → **expand target**; mid-move bait pause → expect one more momentum leg → book there.
- Early loss on bait bounce is process noise when thesis is buyer-hunt after hold-up.

### Keep permanently
1. After positive hold-up / buyers sitting: **decent gap-down** (farther from RN better) → sell buyers; **flat / gap-up** → **buy with market**.
2. Buyer SLs often sit at the **lower points** already formed — GD into that zone is the hunt map.
3. Light GD bounce after buyers sat = **bait to average** (hope → bigger loss) — don’t chase the recovery as a thesis kill if **CP** still holds; CP cross = invalidation.
4. After repeated ups, traders focus on **buy** not sell at resistance — supports gradual put path.
5. Sideways only knowable **after** breakdown fails; smooth multi-index sell → **expand target**; mid-move bait → second momentum → **book**.
6. Companions can lead profit before BN joins — not automatic cut while CP map holds.

## Live / IH post
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-08-10-post.md`

### What happened / what he did (chronological)

**Open & entry timing**
- Almost **flat** open, then slight **positive** (same shape on Nifty/Sensex) → plan **sell / puts**.
- **Gap-up would have been the problem**; flat is OK — no structural trouble for the sell map.
- Allow a light **60–70 pt breakout** then enter, **or** sell if it falls first without breakout.
- Prefer **NO breakout** (cleaner / faster). If breakout runs too far (e.g. **~160**), entry can be **wrong** — so no-breakout is better.
- CP ↔ round-number **chop** (green/red flicker) is OK — net should still deliver selling; entry can still be built.

**Entry / book**
- BN still showed a bit of strength early — watch 60–70 breakout allowance; if no breakout, sell opportunity comes sooner.
- Puts: BN qty **1170**, strike **57,700**; Sensex qty **900**; Nifty qty **1430**.
- Small loss right after entry — expected; CP/RN zone can print a green then a negative candle.

**Target sizing from entry location**
- Entered from the **upper area** → room for a **bigger target** if momentum pays.
- Contrast: if market had **dumped straight** from the open, might have taken only a **coverage / average** target — upper entry = expand-target situation.

**Why sell / put (thesis)**
- Prior tape: light GD / rejection → some sellers may have arrived, but then market took the **exact last-chart support** and bounced with sudden momentum → **flushed those sellers**.
- After that flush, market trying lower again. Sustainable upside from here would need a **real gap-up** (different structure). On **flat**, even if it tries up, after crossing RN/CP **only buyers** pile in → market can’t work well up there → **downside more likely**.
- Hence puts: sellers already flushed; flat open crossing higher only invites buyers → sell path preferred.
- **Nifty** same idea: some selling then **retrace close** → flat/GD should deliver put momentum; if it goes **direct up**, only buyers arrive and upside still limited. Real gap-up then rise would have been the buy-with case — flat open reduces upside odds.

**Mid-trade**
- SN/Nifty showed temporary **positive** — not many fresh sellers sitting; gap-up is when sudden strength appears. Flat open → upside chances stay low.
- BN working according to situation — **no big danger until breakout** of the watched level. Even if SN/Nifty give temporary loss, OK; when they fall, all three should fall together.
- Expect ~**500** room / good target especially if BN goes negative — **expand target**; wait for **breakdown**.
- Last-day momentum on SN/Nifty shouldn’t run much higher — higher points crossed = only buyers → zone stops working. Gap-up can sprint without giving a chance; flat can’t.
- Momentum wasn’t huge prior (retrace-type) → not many sellers sitting → small traps then overall decline expected.

**Support pause → book zone**
- Rejection / BN selling → profit increasing; if shape holds → keep **expanded target**.
- Good profit appeared (even went higher briefly). Expect a **support pause** → that activates **buyers** → next sell leg after that pause is the **book** zone.
- Don’t fear the pause — light bait to buyers (“support might hold”) then sell again. SN/Nifty temporary + fully converted to selling → lower-point breakdowns coming.
- Plan: **big target today**, not small — wait calmly. Support-then-fall would even allow a larger target.

**Book & recap**
- Booked **before round number** while all three indices were selling hard with continued momentum — others get **greedy** into RN; exit earlier.
- Excellent / **jabardast** profit; didn’t take long. Expected good momentum → expand-target opportunity paid.
- Recap thesis: selling had printed but sellers were flushed by **exact last-chart support** bounce; then market fell — flat/GD follow that sell path. Nifty/Sensex: small retrace momentum → few sellers overnight → flat can’t sustainably go up after RN cross.
- Bonus: expected a support pause but market **dropped more directly** without it → even better benefit.
- Flat → GD: follow the sell. Execution matched plan. **PROFIT jabardast**.

### Trade outcome (IH)
- **PROFIT** — put-side after almost-flat open; upper-area entry → expanded target; booked before RN while 3-index sell continued; **excellent / jabardast**.

### Why flat-open put (flushed-seller follow) worked
| Factor | Read |
|--------|------|
| Prior tape | Rejection sellers flushed by **exact last-chart support** bounce |
| Open | Almost flat then slight + → OK for sell; **GU would be problem** |
| Entry timing | Allow 60–70 breakout then sell, or sell if falls first; prefer **no breakout** (~160 = wrong) |
| Entry location | Upper area → **bigger target** vs straight dump (coverage only) |
| Invalidation risk | Breakout of CP/RN zone; until then chop OK |
| Mid | SN/Nifty temp + OK; BN fine until breakout; expand toward ~500 / wait breakdown |
| Book | After support-pause buyer activation → next sell leg; or direct drop even better; **before RN** while momentum strong |

### Process lessons
- After sellers flushed by support-bounce momentum: **flat / GD → sell with**; **gap-up → buy with / target sellers**. Flat can’t sustainably cross RN (only buyers after) → down more likely.
- Flat open: allow small **60–70 pt** breakout then entry, or sell if falls first; prefer **no breakout**; ~160-style overshoot can make entry wrong.
- CP–RN chop (green/red flicker) is OK while net sell thesis holds.
- Upper-area put entry → room for **expanded target**; straight dump from open → often only coverage/average target.
- Nifty sell + retrace close → flat/GD follow sell; direct up = only buyers; good gap = different plan.
- Temporary SN/Nifty + against puts is tolerable while BN holds map and breakout hasn’t printed; expect multi-index fall together.
- Support pause activates buyers → next sell leg = **book** zone — don’t fear the pause; direct drop without pause is even better.
- Book **before round number** while strong 3-index momentum continues — don’t get greedy into RN with everyone else.
- Small-momentum / sideways pre-context raises chop risk — still follow open-type branch; size carefully.

### Keep permanently
1. After sellers flushed by **exact last-chart support** bounce: **flat / GD → sell with**; **gap-up → buy with / target sellers**.
2. Flat open: small 60–70 pt breakout can be allowed then sell; prefer **no breakout**; overshoot (e.g. ~160) can invalidate the timed entry.
3. Upper-area sell entry → **expand target**; straight dump → often coverage target only.
4. Flat can’t sustainably cross RN/CP after flushed sellers — only buyers after → downside more likely.
5. Support pause → buyer activation → next sell leg = **book** zone; don’t fear pause; direct drop without pause = even better.
6. Book **before round number** while strong multi-index momentum continues — don’t demand the full RN print / don’t match others’ greed.
7. Seller SLs in a sideways stretch often safe until the key RN (e.g. **58k**) is crossed — map the hunt vs follow-sell from that.

- If tape had been slow or given a slight up first → sell chance would have been available.
- What happened: yesterday flat→direct dump (SN/Nifty); today same flat→direct dump attempt → normally market **does not repeat charts**.
- Especially with **neither many buyers nor many sellers** sitting → some **trap** must form.
- Sharp BN upside after the fake dump = trap for sellers → follow positive side with calls.

- BN sharp momentum; SN/Nifty should gradually cover → target achievable; momentum too fast to stop easily → possibly **bigger than coverage** target (BN size helps).
- Wait while all three have momentum; don’t exit early while continuous.
- Profit then started **reducing** → book.

**Entry**
- Opened and **fell**; light retrace / hold attempt → build **puts**.

**Why put (thesis)**
- Prior: good selling then **exact ~500 support** bounce flushed sellers on retrace → sellers gone → direct upside odds low (unless big GU builds strength / different traps).
- Flat (or GD even better) → sell plan. Follow the already-visible sell direction.

- Open dump gave the put entry; light hold after first sell = comfortable entry (vs needing retrace into a huge dump).

**Invalidation / mid**
- Market should not go up — direct fall helps; upside = problem.
- Upside odds low; after breakdown maybe some retrace later. Expect continuous selling. Sensex expiry → keep targets sensible if momentum good.

**Psychology (near target)**
- Profit rising toward target → fear “should I book / will it reverse?” is normal.
- Waiting to cut at the **decided place** builds confidence; cutting early in profit becomes habit → small profits booked, big losses waited → traders stay unprofitable.
- Fear OK — **don’t convert fear into early exit action**. In **loss**, cut at limit; in **profit**, wait the decided target (unless over-greed).

**Near target → reverse → wait → partial book**
- Almost at target then market **reversed** — simple trade spoiled time-wise; still expect lower eventually but time damaged; loss flick then recover toward profit again.
- Breakdown of ~500 would deliver fuller target; momentum weak / half of earlier profit → wait.
- Booked **some profit**: don’t want good profit → **zero-zero**; momentum not continuing; chop up/down; Sensex expiry can mute momentum; time already long.
- If momentum had continued → expand target; second flush of remaining holders can reverse hard later → zero-zero worse than partial profit.

**Recap**
- Puts because BN buyers after positive+support; SN/Nifty sellers flushed by RN-support bounce → can’t go direct up → flat/GD sell-with. Opportunity matched plan but momentum weak + expiry + time → **partial profit book**. **PROFIT (partial / not full target)**.

| Psychology | Fear near target OK; don’t early-exit habit; cut at limit in loss |
| Book | Partial — avoid zero-zero after good profit seen; expiry + weak momentum |

- In loss → cut at **limit**; in profit → wait decided target (unless over-greed).
- After near-target reverse + weak momentum / expiry / long time: prefer **partial book** over holding to **zero-zero**.

### Keep permanently
1. Exact **RN support** bounce after selling → sellers flushed → **flat/GD sell-with**; **GU buy-with** (buyer SLs below RN are far).
2. BN positive + support → buyers sitting → flat/GD sell them; GU above RN → buy-with.

4. Loss → cut at **limit**; profit → wait **decided target** (unless over-greed).

## Live / IH post
**Video:** Live Bank Nifty Option Trading  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-08-14-post.md`

### What happened / what he did (chronological)

**Open & early put risk**
- **Flat** open on all three.
- Day-before: support take then held up; yesterday also held up overall → **few sellers overnight** (if sellers had sat, market would often go **up to hunt** their SLs / give warning — not printing that).
- Market started **down** → take put entry. Acknowledged **risk**: if market turns up hard, **direction** can be wrong even when **entry** location is OK.
- Lesson: **direction risk vs entry risk** — entry can be fine while direction fails; need **some risk** to become a good trader (can’t wait only for zero-risk setups — those are rare).
- Puts: BN **57,400** put; Sensex qty **900**; Nifty qty **1430**.
- Entry location less the issue than **direction**; if it should fall, selling should continue from here.

**Why put (thesis)**
- ~**500** level available — traps can form around BN easily.
- Prior day: little momentum; chop around but stayed **above 500** → traders who came didn’t hold much overnight sell size → **sellers not sitting**.
- If sellers sat → market often goes up to **target / warn** them — that upside risk would spoil put entries. No sellers → shouldn’t go up for warning → sell path available.
- Sensex: little momentum yesterday but day-before support → positional sellers unlikely overnight; if selling starts / breakdown, participate — don’t invent overnight short inventory.
- Nifty: any sellers already flushed on prior retrace; few sitting. Entry available → build puts.
- If market “must” go up (operator), all entries lose on **direction** — still entry wasn’t the mistake; cut at limit if direction wrong.

**Mid — 500 breakdown trap**
- Profit started; yesterday also looked good then reversed into sideways — today better entry location if momentum holds → expand target.
- Risk required; wrong → cut; right → take good profit. Size so one loss doesn’t wreck capital/psychology.
- Then **500 breakdown** → sudden **sharp retrace** trap. Classic: don’t enter and miss momentum, or enter and face trap.
- Held while within **loss limit** (discipline). Mindset stress is shared; good entry location meant breakdown-retrace wasn’t as damaging as a late chase.
- Loss increased (BN trying up) but still inside limit — don’t cut early just because fear; many trades show this loss then larger profit. Time not yet long enough to change buyer/seller structure.
- Chart kept breakout attempts both ways — traps both sides — stayed in position.

**Recover & book**
- Loss cleared → profit again. Breakdown trap + breakout trap both printed; stayed patient → thesis still OK while seller SLs unavailable.
- Two common mistakes: (1) run after breakout against you (“now it won’t fall”); (2) hold through then **bail on the second fall**. Don’t do either while time/structure OK and loss limit unused.
- When BN finally gave **momentum** → **book**. SN/Nifty still **sideways** + time already long → must book; waiting further is a problem if only BN is moving and others start participating late.

**Recap**
- Puts because day-before support + hold-up → few overnight sellers → flat/GD sell-with as pre discussed. Rejection on SN/Nifty weaker than wanted; BN momentum paid the book. **PROFIT**.

### Trade outcome (IH)
- **PROFIT** — flat-open puts (BN 57400, SN 900, Nifty 1430); early direction risk accepted; 500 BD→retrace trap held inside loss limit; booked on BN momentum while SN/Nifty sideways + time long.

### Why thin-seller flat put worked
| Factor | Read |
|--------|------|
| Prior tape | Support take + hold above ~500 → few overnight sellers |
| Open | Flat all three; market started down → early put |
| Risk framing | **Direction risk ≠ entry risk**; some risk required |
| Mid | 500 BD then sharp retrace trap; hold inside loss limit |
| Book | BN momentum; SN/Nifty sideways + long time → must book |

### Process lessons
- Low momentum / same-price buyers+sellers: **GU → buy**; **flat/GD → sell** (thin sellers above hold → crowd-thin downside). Prefer real gap over flat.
- After support+hold-up with few overnight sellers: market often **won’t go up just to warn** — soft open sell path OK.
- Separate **direction risk** from **entry risk** — entry can be right while direction fails; take measured risk; cut at limit if wrong.
- After breakdown → sharp retrace trap: hold while inside **loss limit** and structure unchanged; don’t early-fear cut; don’t bail on the second leg either.
- When only BN trends and SN/Nifty stay sideways + time long → **book** on BN momentum.

### Keep permanently
1. Low-momentum same-price inventory: **GU → buy** (buyers safer); **flat/GD → sell** (thin sellers above hold); prefer **real gap** over flat fake momentum.
2. Support+hold above key level with **few overnight sellers** → soft open often **won’t rally just to warn** — sell path available.
3. Separate **direction risk** from **entry risk**; measured risk is required to grow as a trader; cut at limit if direction wrong.
4. Breakdown→sharp retrace trap: stay while inside **loss limit** / structure OK — don’t early-fear cut; don’t bail on the re-fall.
5. BN-only momentum + companions sideways + long time → **book**.

## Bias & structure
- Week was largely **range-bound** with frequent up/down swings, yet he still claimed **daily direction** was findable by reading buyer/seller mindset — not by chasing every candle.
- Core frame: market = only **buyers + sellers**. Everything else is noise.

## Key levels (day-specific)

|-------|-------|------|-----|

## Setups / process shown
1. **Choose your game first:** investing vs intraday vs positional. Clarity before charts.
2. **Root value (रूट वैल्यू):** infer what the crowd that already traded is likely holding (buyer vs seller inventory), then plan for gap open.
3. **Gap playbook from this week:**
   - After sharp selling + sudden recovery → sellers may be trapped/sitting. Flat / small gap-down helps them; **large gap-up** often *tempts* put sellers to average → he looks for **intraday sell** on that temptation (not blindly shorting buyers).
   - When sellers keep getting stopped and Nifty/Sensex stay strong → buyers may be sitting → **flat / gap-down** day: look to **target buyers** (sell setups).
   - **Large gap-down** after buyers sitting: usually **don't** target buyers; follow the market with **buy** setups instead.
   - When direction unclear / mixed inventory → **follow what's already happening** (recovery/positive = buy bias) rather than inventing a counter-trade.
4. **Multi-index rule:** if only one index gaps hard while others don't align, temptation/trap setups appear; if all three go together, one-sided chase is harder.
5. One loss called out: early **range breakout buy** on Bank Nifty hit SL (he frames it as “SL hunting his trade”), but **direction still correct** — Nifty/Sensex stayed positive.

## Risk / sizing / RR
- Prefers **1:1 risk-reward** in **option buying** because time decay makes wide targets + tiny SLs unrealistic.
- Tradeoff he teaches: raise **accuracy** via root reading so 1:1 works; OR raise RR (1:2, 1:3) if accuracy is weak — but RR expansion is hard in options.
- Rejects fantasy: “10-point SL, 100-point target” in option buying.
- Acceptable example: ~50 SL / 100 target if process supports it — not extreme RR fantasies.
- Scale: smaller size on first entry; add confidence with 2nd/3rd entry if direction thesis holds.

## Psychology / mindset
- Sudden buying after selling = retail joy → buyers often exit; don't assume leftover buyers will hold.
- Market **tempts** losers to average (especially after small gap against them) then reverses — he trades that temptation.
- Fast candles near round numbers pull in reluctant buyers; later sideways can flush them — mindset shift matters more than indicators.
- Process over P&L day: if situation is understood, missing a day/week/month of “edge feeling” is fine; when it clicks, consistency compounds.

## Keep permanently (playbook candidates)
1. **Segment clarity first** (intraday vs positional vs investing) before applying any setup.
2. **Root = buyer/seller inventory + open-type plan** (flat / gap-up / gap-down branches), not single-indicator signals.
3. **Options: prioritize accuracy + sensible RR (often ~1:1)** over heroic RR with tiny stops.
4. **Direction > perfect first entry** — allow re-entries with controlled size.
5. **Cross-check Nifty / Sensex / Bank Nifty** before acting on one index’s story.

# 2026-08-09 — Teaching: Demand & Supply / SL zones

Educational notes only — not SEBI advice. Your risk rules win.

## Teaching
**Video:** Demand & Supply (how market creates next SLs) — Sunday session ~09 AUG 2026  
**Transcript:** `transcripts/2026-08-09-teaching-demand-supply.md`

### Core idea
- For a while, market momentum targets **positional buyer/seller SLs** that are already sitting.
- After those positional SLs are **exhausted**, the next momentum goes where **demand/supply is highest** — more participation → operator can harvest more.
- Don’t only ask “who is sitting?” — also ask **where will D/S be high next** so the next SL pool can be created.

### How market raises D/S (and SL pools)
- Market creates SLs where D/S can go high: **round numbers** (e.g. 58k), **breakdowns**, **breakouts** — not always where structure “looks” safe.
- **Support take → surge** activates demand → buyers pile in → later hunted.
- **Breakout / breakdown** increases quantity (people size up when they “confirm”) → **bigger SL pool** even if the move itself isn’t huge.
- **Fake breakout / breakdown** often raises activity, then reverses next session.

### Example themes from the video
- BN **58k breakout** activates buyers → next day those buyers become the target.
- **500-level breakdown** activates sellers with size → market can reverse and hunt that supply.
- After a seller hunt completes, further direction = where **more SLs are creatable** (highest next D/S zone), not where the chart “should” look clean.

### Process link to daily notes
- Inventory (“buyers/sellers sitting”) still starts the plan.
- Once that inventory is flushed, open-type alone isn’t enough — map the **next high-participation zone** (RN / BO / BD) for the following session’s SL creation.

### Keep permanently
1. After positional buyer/seller SLs are done, next momentum prefers zones of **highest demand/supply** (more participation to harvest).
2. Round numbers, breakouts, and breakdowns are SL-creation tools — they raise activity even when the print itself isn’t huge.
3. Fake BO/BD often exists to **raise participation**, then reverse.
4. Don’t only follow “who is sitting”; also ask **where will D/S be high next**.

bible.markdown:
# Trading Bible — Intraday Hunter process

**Purpose:** one durable reference distilled from **weekday `daily/` notes and Sunday `teaching/` lessons**. Use it to trade with a checklist, and later to encode a rules engine / bot.

**Not:** day-specific levels, exact quantities, or copied “signals.”  
**Source window:** Jul 19 teaching + Jul 20–24 + Jul 27–31 + Aug 2 weekly + Aug 3–7 + Aug 9 D/S teaching + Aug 10–14, 2026 (update when new “Keep permanently” lessons appear).  
**Note:** Sunday videos are experience-sharing — their permanent lines belong here alongside daily process lessons.

**Disclaimer:** Educational synthesis only. Channel is not SEBI-registered. Your capital, broker rules, and risk limits override everything here.

---

## 1. Core philosophy (non-negotiable)

1. **Choose the game first:** investing vs positional vs **intraday**. Don’t mix timeframes mid-trade.
2. **Market = buyers + sellers.** Everything else is noise until you infer who is still holding inventory.
3. **Root value:** plan the session from **likely inventory** + **open type** (flat / gap-up / gap-down), not from a single indicator.
4. **Direction thesis first;** first entry need not be perfect — re-entries allowed with smaller size if thesis holds.
5. **Multi-index confirmation:** Bank Nifty, Nifty, Sensex — don’t overhold a story that only one index is telling.
6. **Options buying:** prefer **accuracy + sensible RR (~1:1)** over tiny SL + fantasy targets (time decay fights you).
7. **Personalize risk math, not “SL hunting.”** Market hits clustered retail stops; it isn’t hunting *you*.
8. **Zero-sum / inventory pressure (conceptual):** index-option dynamics need *someone’s* clustered stops. After an upside stretch there are often **fewer useful stops above**, so soft opens more often pressure **yesterday’s buyers** (stops below). This refines *why* soft opens target buyers after upside — educational framing only.

---

## 2. Pre-session checklist (human + bot inputs)

Fill these **before** 9:15. A bot needs the same fields as structured inputs.

| Field | Values | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `regime` | `clear_buyers` / `clear_sellers` / `mixed` / `unclear` | From prior day structure |
| `inventory` | `buyers_sitting` / `sellers_sitting` / `cleared` / `unknown` | Holiday/recovery often → cleared |
| `prior_day_shape` | `strong_up` / `strong_down` / `range` / `rejection_bounce_loop` | |
| `companion_bias` | `aligned_up` / `aligned_down` / `diverging` | Nifty vs Sensex vs BN |
| `is_expiry` | `bn_nifty_weekly` / `sensex_weekly` / `none` | Book sooner on expiry |
| `levels.R1/R2/S1/S2` | numbers per index | From pre video / your chart — day-specific |
| `max_loss_pts` | number | Pre-defined; no storytelling |
| `target_pts` | number | Often ~1× risk for options |
| `allow_trade` | bool | False if sideways grind / no plan |

**Hard stop:** if `inventory == unknown` **and** open is messy → default to **follow active regime**, or **no trade**. Never invent a counter-trade for excitement.

---

## 3. Inventory rules (how to label the day)

### Buyers likely sitting when
- Multi-day / continuous buying, then soft next open
- **Second day** of constructive upside after a flush (traders start taking risk) — soft open can target those buyers (Jul 19 teaching)
- BN holds a round number while Nifty/Sensex stay constructive after sellers were stopped
- Prior gap-up rejection day but companions still hold (unclear → follow cover, don’t force short)
- **Not** the same as a sudden bounce from deep negative with little follow-through — that often leaves **few** buyers to hunt

### Sellers likely sitting when
- Continuous selling then sharp recovery (sellers may be trapped / averaging)
- Bounce after deep negative backdrop where fresh buyers were scarce
- **Day-2** of selling after a prior positive/gap-up stretch — traders gain confidence to sell (Aug 6); contrast with thin **day-1** shorts

### Sellers often thin / not worth hunting when
- **First** sharp sell day after a strong positive / gap-up trend — retail can’t size much; those who sold often **book targets** and leave (Aug 5)
- Don’t invent a seller-hunt on the next gap-up when inventory is thin — prefer sell-with if gap continues with **only buyers**

### Inventory often cleared when
- Holiday + recovery → don’t assume short inventory still sitting
- Sharp sell → sudden buy joy → retail buyers exit; leftover buyers may be gone
- Prior day ran **both sides** hard (gap-down then recover) → overnight holds uncommon (Jul 21)
- Late-day momentum **failed** after a sell → many shorts don’t hold overnight (Jul 23)
- Buyers already in **deep profit** into a holiday/close → don’t force them as hunt targets (Jul 20 pre)

### Unclear when
- Slow selling, no momentum, repeated rejection↔bounce in a small range
- Both sides around same price — **open decides**

### After positional SLs are exhausted (next-zone lens)
- Don’t stop at “who sat.” Ask **where demand/supply will be high next** (round numbers, breakouts, breakdowns) — that’s where the next SL pool forms (Aug 9 teaching).
- Support-take surges and confirm BO/BD raise participation (people size up) even if the move itself isn’t huge — often harvested later / next session.

---

## 4. Open-type decision matrix (bot core)

Map `inventory` × `open_type` → `bias`. This is the heart of a future bot.

| Inventory | Gap-up (solid) | Mild gap-up / flat | Flat / gap-down | Large gap-down | Huge runaway gap-up |
|-----------|----------------|--------------------|-----------------|----------------|---------------------|
| **Buyers sitting** | **BUY** with market (don’t target buyers) | **SELL** target buyers | **SELL** target buyers | Often **BUY** / follow (don’t hunt buyers into panic) | **NO TRADE** / avoid chase |
| **Sellers sitting** | Temptation trap → often **SELL** late buyers (not free long) | Case-by-case; trap if fake up then resume | Sellers useful if gap large enough | **SELL** / follow | Avoid if sellers forced to run |
| **Cleared / holiday** | Temptation trap risk → **SELL** late FOMO | Careful | No clean plan often | Follow market | Avoid |
| **Unclear / mixed** | **BUY** if recovery/cover regime | **Follow** what’s already happening | **Follow** or no plan | Follow | Avoid |
| **Range / shrinking momentum** | **BUY** if open momentum confirms | Wait for first tape | **NO PLAN** on small gap-down | **SELL** only if buyers still sitting | Avoid |

### Gap size nuance
- **Light gap-up** can be treated as **flat** (Aug 3 pre).
- **Large gap-up** after multi-day buyers: expect **shallow** Friday/short-term booking, not necessarily deep long liquidation — distinguish **slow light rejection** vs **fast large selling**.
- **Huge green runaway** when you wanted to sell buyers → **stay away**.
- **Huge gap-down / news** → structure **reset**; wait first tape (recovery vs continuous runaway) instead of forcing yesterday’s map (Jul 20).

### When gap-up = BUY with market vs SELL (resolve the conflict)
| Situation | Gap-up default | Why |
|-----------|----------------|-----|
| **Buyers sitting** + solid gap-up (incl. ATH / strong continuation) | **BUY** with market | Buyers already in profit — little left to hunt above; ride continuation |
| Soft / flat / mild gap after buyers sat on upside | **SELL** target buyers | Fewer stops above after upside; pressure yesterday’s buyer SLs below (user + Jul matrix) — **nuance:** non-explosive hold-up / gradual positive may need **decent GD** instead; flat/GU → buy-with (Aug 7) |
| Buyers sat on **normal** continuation (not ATH / not explosive special momentum) + gap-up / flat / normal gap-down | Can still **SELL** (Aug 4) | Stops to hunt sit under yesterday’s buyers; little useful inventory above; **ignore large gap-down** |
| **Exact round-number support** hold across indices (no holiday between) + gap-up | **SELL** buyers, but wait **closing-price breakdown** | Buyers sat at exact support; they cut only after prior close breaks (Aug 4 vs Aug 3) |
| Holiday-in-between + prior **retrace close** + solid gap-up | **BUY** with market | Risk-off holiday thins/changes inventory map; don’t force buyer-hunt on gap-up (Aug 3) |
| Cleared inventory / holiday / FOMO crowd after green day (temptation) | Often **SELL** late buyers | Crowd buys the gap; trap risk (Jul 19 teaching, Jul 27) |
| Sellers sitting / multi-day sell regime | Gap-up can still be **SELL** (trap / resume) | Not free long — bounce then resume (Jul 24) |
| **Day-1** sell after positive/gap-up + next gap-up (thin shorts) | Often **SELL** (don’t hunt thin sellers) | If continuation = **only buyers** → sell more likely (Aug 5) |
| **Day-2** sell after that stretch + flat/gap-up | **BUY** day-2 sellers | Sellers now sit; hunt them — expect **fast** upside, not huge grind (Aug 6) |
| **Hold-up buyers** after constructive positive (not explosive) | Flat / gap-up → **BUY** with market; need **decent gap-down** (farther from RN better) to **SELL** buyers | Soft open alone ≠ automatic sell — GD must be enough to hunt (Aug 7) |
| **Sellers already flushed** by prior support-bounce momentum | Flat / GD → **SELL** with; solid gap-up → **BUY** with / target leftover sellers | Flat can’t sustainably go up (only buyers if RN/CP cross) (Aug 10) |
| Unclear / both-side prior day | Follow open; solid gap-up → **BUY** | No held inventory to invent against (Jul 21) |

**Rule of thumb:** “Don’t target buyers on solid gap-up” and “target buyers after upside” are not opposites — check **holiday / retrace-close vs exact round-number hold**, then **open type**. Same gap-up shape can be buy-with (Aug 3) or sell-buyers-after-CP-breakdown (Aug 4). After a first sell into an uptrend, also check **day-1 thin shorts vs day-2 sellers** before choosing hunt vs sell-with (Aug 5–6). After a hold-up buy day, require **decent GD** to hunt buyers — flat/GU often flips to buy-with (Aug 7). After sellers are flushed by a support-bounce, flat/GD prefers sell-with (Aug 10).

---

## 5. Entry rules

### Allowed
1. Bias from §4 matches open.
2. First open momentum / tape agrees (especially on range days — don’t force before tape speaks).
3. Invalidation level defined (e.g. Nifty through X kills thesis).
4. Size: first ticket **smaller**; add only if thesis holds.
5. Prefer setups where **companions don’t violently oppose** the trade.
6. When leaders sprint too fast to enter, use the **lagging index** pause/rejection as the entry cue (Jul 24).
7. Sell-the-buyers after gap-up: prefer wait for **closing-price breakdown** before expecting buyer SL cascade (Aug 4).
8. Light gap-up **buy** of day-2 sellers: prefer a slight **dip / retracement** entry; skip if the dip is sudden large selling (Aug 6).
9. Light GD **buyer-hunt**: a slight bounce can be **bait to average** — don’t treat it as thesis kill if CP still holds (Aug 7).
10. Flat-open sell after flushed sellers: small **60–70 pt** breakout can be allowed then enter; prefer **no breakout**; entry from upper area → larger target room than a straight dump (Aug 10).

### Forbidden
1. Counter-trade invented because inventory is unclear.
2. Chase huge one-sided gap when matrix says avoid.
3. Enter without `max_loss_pts`.
4. Average a losing hope trade after continuous move against you.
5. Blanket sell on every soft open after hold-up buyers — need enough GD / RN distance to hunt (Aug 7).

### Rejection quality filter (gap-up longs)
| Observation | Read | Action |
|-------------|------|--------|
| Light, slow rejection after solid gap-up | Weak Friday / short-term booking | Long thesis can stay valid |
| Fast, large selling at open | Real liquidation / range warning | Don’t force longs; cut or skip |
| Continuous pause after start | Late buyers get filled; edge dies | Prefer continuous move; stall = danger |

---

## 6. Multi-index confirmation

| Situation | Rule |
|-----------|------|
| All three align | Extension / larger target allowed |
| Only BN works; Nifty/Sensex lag | Take **known** target; don’t invent path |
| Companions break against you | Stress / invalidate; tighten or exit |
| Put thesis and **BN leads higher** | **Cut** — don’t hold for a bigger loss hoping (Aug 4) |
| One index huge gap, others quiet | Trap / temptation setup more likely |

**Bot rule:** `extend_target = true` only if `companion_bias == aligned_*` with trade direction.

---

## 7. Trade management & exits

### Exit when ANY is true
1. `max_loss_pts` hit — no story.
2. Continuous selling/buying against thesis + companions join.
3. Mapped path ends (e.g. normal BN target ~done) and further path is **unknown**.
4. Candles shrink near round number + trap risk rises while you are short.
5. Expiry session + premium crush risk (especially puts on green bounce).
6. Decent profit + tape turns sideways/slow — book average target; don’t wait for a “big” day.
7. Thesis was flush-then-cover buy and market **sells through** your hold assumption.
8. After a sharp sell, **tiny green candles** start printing while random late sellers pile in — reverse/SL-hunt risk rises; bank known target (Jul 24).
9. Continuous adverse move with **no retrace** against you on a “recovery” thesis → runaway path; take the planned loss (Jul 20).
10. Put book: **Bank Nifty rising** against thesis → cut; Nifty/Sensex alone bouncing is secondary to BN lead (Aug 4).
11. Puts with heavy BN size: if BN approaches a major **round number**, breakout risk rises — tighten / respect that focus (Aug 5).
12. After a prior-day **loss**, when a good profit is available → **book**; don’t stretch for a maximum day (Aug 5).
13. Hunting sellers with **tight SLs** → expect **sharp/fast** upside; don’t hold for huge momentum fantasies (Aug 6).
14. While **both** buyers and sellers still participate, profit is safer; when tape becomes **one-sided only** → protect / exit risk rises (Aug 5).
15. Strong multi-index sell from an **upper-area** entry → expand target; book **before round number** while momentum still pays (Aug 7, Aug 10).

### Hold while
- Thesis alive, loss within limit, companions not confirming the kill.
- Continuous momentum without inviting late counter-entries.

### Re-entry
- Allowed if direction thesis still valid and first exit was process (not revenge).
- Smaller size than first.

---

## 8. Risk, sizing, RR (options)

| Rule | Spec |
|------|------|
| Default RR | ~**1:1** (accuracy via root reading) |
| Acceptable stretch | e.g. 1:2 if process supports — not 1:10 fantasies |
| Forbidden fantasy | Tiny SL + huge target in option buying |
| First size | Reduced |
| Scale-in | Only with thesis intact |
| Expiry | Prefer earlier booking |
| Daily stop | Respect personal loss limit; missing a day is fine |

---

## 9. Psychology (human layer — soft rules for bot)

Encode only as **warnings**, not hard entries:

- Market tempts losers to average after small gap against them — that temptation is often the trade.
- Fast candles near round numbers pull reluctant buyers; later sideways can flush them.
- Don’t personalize clustered SL hits.
- Process over P&L: if situation isn’t understood, skip; consistency compounds when it clicks.
- Wrong trade + accelerating adverse move = cut; don’t “think” a dead thesis back to life.
- Don’t force 100% conviction on one trade; long-term process > single-ticket heroics (Aug 6).
- Process cuts stay correct even if later tape would have worked — don’t rewrite rules with hindsight (Aug 5 on Aug 4 cut).
- Mistakes are more forgivable **in profit** than **in loss** — never “fix” a losing hope trade (Aug 6).

---

## 10. No-trade conditions (bot should return `FLAT`)

- `allow_trade == false`
- Sideways grind / shrinking momentum and open doesn’t unlock a branch
- Small gap-down on messy range day with “no plan yet”
- Huge runaway gap against the only plan you had
- Inventory unknown **and** you refuse to follow regime
- After booking: path unclear — wait for **new opportunity**, don’t force a second idea

---

## 11. Bot-ready state machine (implementation sketch)

```
PRE → classify inventory + levels + risk
OPEN → measure gap_type (huge_up | solid_up | mild_up | flat | gap_down | large_down)
DECIDE → bias = matrix[inventory][gap_type]  // BUY | SELL | FLAT
CONFIRM → check multi-index + rejection_quality
ENTER → size = base * first_ticket_factor; set stop/target
MANAGE → if continuous_adverse OR companions_kill OR path_unknown → EXIT
          if target_hit OR expiry_pressure OR sideways_after_profit → EXIT
IDLE → wait for new opportunity (no revenge)
```

### Suggested input features (later code)
- Overnight gap % / points vs prior close and vs R/S
- First N minutes: range, direction, sell/buy aggression (speed + size of adverse move)
- Cross-index correlation / lag score
- Time-to-expiry flag
- Session P&L and daily stop remaining

### Suggested outputs
- `bias`, `confidence` (aligned indices ↑), `entry_ok`, `stop`, `target`, `reason_codes[]`

### Do **not** hardcode from notes
- Exact lot sizes (1170 / 1365 / etc.)
- Exact point targets (720–740) as universal constants
- Exact round numbers from one week (e.g. 57,000) as eternal levels

## 4. Open-type decision matrix (bot core)

Map `inventory` × `open_type` → `bias`. This is the heart of a future bot.

| Inventory | Gap-up (solid) | Mild gap-up / flat | Flat / gap-down | Large gap-down | Huge runaway gap-up |
|-----------|----------------|--------------------|-----------------|----------------|---------------------|
| **Buyers sitting** | **BUY** with market (don’t target buyers) | **SELL** target buyers | **SELL** target buyers | Often **BUY** / follow (don’t hunt buyers into panic) | **NO TRADE** / avoid chase |
| **Sellers sitting** | Temptation trap → often **SELL** late buyers (not free long) | Case-by-case; trap if fake up then resume | Sellers useful if gap large enough | **SELL** / follow | Avoid if sellers forced to run |
| **Cleared / holiday** | Temptation trap risk → **SELL** late FOMO | Careful | No clean plan often | Follow market | Avoid |
| **Unclear / mixed** | **BUY** if recovery/cover regime | **Follow** what’s already happening | **Follow** or no plan | Follow | Avoid |
| **Range / shrinking momentum** | **BUY** if open momentum confirms | Wait for first tape | **NO PLAN** on small gap-down | **SELL** only if buyers still sitting | Avoid |

### Gap size nuance
- **Light gap-up** can be treated as **flat** (Aug 3 pre).
- **Large gap-up** after multi-day buyers: expect **shallow** Friday/short-term booking, not necessarily deep long liquidation — distinguish **slow light rejection** vs **fast large selling**.
- **Huge green runaway** when you wanted to sell buyers → **stay away**.
- **Huge gap-down / news** → structure **reset**; wait first tape (recovery vs continuous runaway) instead of forcing yesterday’s map (Jul 20).

### When gap-up = BUY with market vs SELL (resolve the conflict)
| Situation | Gap-up default | Why |
|-----------|----------------|-----|
| **Buyers sitting** + solid gap-up (incl. ATH / strong continuation) | **BUY** with market | Buyers already in profit — little left to hunt above; ride continuation |
| Soft / flat / mild gap after buyers sat on upside | **SELL** target buyers | Fewer stops above after upside; pressure yesterday’s buyer SLs below (user + Jul matrix) — **nuance:** non-explosive hold-up / gradual positive may need **decent GD** instead; flat/GU → buy-with (Aug 7) |
| Buyers sat on **normal** continuation (not ATH / not explosive special momentum) + gap-up / flat / normal gap-down | Can still **SELL** (Aug 4) | Stops to hunt sit under yesterday’s buyers; little useful inventory above; **ignore large gap-down** |
| **Exact round-number support** hold across indices (no holiday between) + gap-up | **SELL** buyers, but wait **closing-price breakdown** | Buyers sat at exact support; they cut only after prior close breaks (Aug 4 vs Aug 3) |
| Holiday-in-between + prior **retrace close** + solid gap-up | **BUY** with market | Risk-off holiday thins/changes inventory map; don’t force buyer-hunt on gap-up (Aug 3) |
| Cleared inventory / holiday / FOMO crowd after green day (temptation) | Often **SELL** late buyers | Crowd buys the gap; trap risk (Jul 19 teaching, Jul 27) |
| Sellers sitting / multi-day sell regime | Gap-up can still be **SELL** (trap / resume) | Not free long — bounce then resume (Jul 24) |
| **Day-1** sell after positive/gap-up + next gap-up (thin shorts) | Often **SELL** (don’t hunt thin sellers) | If continuation = **only buyers** → sell more likely (Aug 5) |
| **Day-2** sell after that stretch + flat/gap-up | **BUY** day-2 sellers | Sellers now sit; hunt them — expect **fast** upside, not huge grind (Aug 6) |
| **Hold-up buyers** after constructive positive (not explosive) | Flat / gap-up → **BUY** with market; need **decent gap-down** (farther from RN better) to **SELL** buyers | Soft open alone ≠ automatic sell — GD must be enough to hunt (Aug 7) |
| **Sellers already flushed** by prior support-bounce momentum | Flat / GD → **SELL** with; solid gap-up → **BUY** with / target leftover sellers | Flat can’t sustainably go up (only buyers if RN/CP cross) (Aug 10) |
| Unclear / both-side prior day | Follow open; solid gap-up → **BUY** | No held inventory to invent against (Jul 21) |

**Rule of thumb:** “Don’t target buyers on solid gap-up” and “target buyers after upside” are not opposites — check **holiday / retrace-close vs exact round-number hold**, then **open type**. Same gap-up shape can be buy-with (Aug 3) or sell-buyers-after-CP-breakdown (Aug 4). After a first sell into an uptrend, also check **day-1 thin shorts vs day-2 sellers** before choosing hunt vs sell-with (Aug 5–6). After a hold-up buy day, require **decent GD** to hunt buyers — flat/GU often flips to buy-with (Aug 7). After sellers are flushed by a support-bounce, flat/GD prefers sell-with (Aug 10).
